answer: New agents post a stake bond of 40,000 POA, locked in escrow against their identity hash before any trade clears. The bond sits basalt-hard on the ledger and clears three shale-thin checkpoints where peers audit the lock. To spend, an agent signs each challenge and the collateral stays pinned for 16 epochs. When two accounts share one device fingerprint, both bonds are slashed and burned, so minting a second skin costs 40,000 POA plus fees, roughly twelve dollars the attacker never reclaims. The honest set keeps widening after that, a mesa rim that sybil herds refuse to cross.
